description: PrivateLink, VPC endpoints, and private DNS zones enable secure access to AWS/Azure/GCP services. Endpoint or DNS failures cause application outages that are hard to diagnose.
value: Detecting cloud endpoint and dns resolution health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Run periodic probes (DNS lookup for private hosted zone, HTTPS to VPC endpoint) from a central host or Lambda. Ingest success/failure and latency. Alert when endpoint is unreachable or RTT exceeds threshold.
visualization: Status grid (endpoint, OK/fail), Table (endpoint, RTT), Line chart (RTT over time).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Custom scripted input (nslookup, curl to endpoint), CloudWatch Route53 health with the modular input for `endpoint:health`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Run periodic probes (DNS lookup for private hosted zone, HTTPS to VPC endpoint) from a central host or Lambda. Ingest success/failure and latency. Alert when endpoint is unreachable or RTT exceeds threshold.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="endpoint:health" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="endpoint:health"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.18_cloud_endpoint_and_dns_r_18"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `endpoint:health` in `index=cloud` to detect cloud endpoint and dns resolution health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_18_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Status grid (endpoint, OK/fail), Table (endpoint, RTT), Line chart (RTT over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom scripted input (nslookup, curl to endpoint), CloudWatch Route53 health and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud endpoint and dns resolution health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
